intro: Meares Island lies in Clayoquot Sound off Tofino on Vancouver Island's west coast. Its Big Tree Trail is a boardwalk through old-growth rainforest where western redcedars are described as up to 1,500 years old. The Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks guardians manage the trail, and you reach the island by a short water taxi ride from Tofino. Seeing the trail's trees from the boardwalk costs nothing beyond that.

trees.story:
On Meares Island, across the water from Tofino, a boardwalk threads through old-growth rainforest where western redcedars grow so large that two people with outstretched arms cannot reach round one. Tourism pages describe the trail's cedars as up to 1,500 years old, and the best known tree on it, the Hanging Garden Tree, is given a circumference of about 18.3 metres. We do not know which of the big cedars this reader's photograph shows, and no age has been measured for it, so we give none.

The photograph shows the reason to make the trip. Two broad trunks have fused at the base into one flared, root-buttressed mass, with thick brown fluted bark, and they lean apart as they rise into the dark canopy. Two visitors stand at the foot with arms spread, each barely covering a quarter of the width. Moss grows on the bark and other trees stand close behind.

The trail is on Tla-o-qui-aht territory, and the Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks guardians now manage it. There is no road to the island. Visitors come by water taxi from Tofino and walk a boardwalk loop of about three and a half to four kilometres. Check the current rules and any trail fee before going.
